samples.summary: Frontend header/footer `marginFromEdge` read was left without the NaN guard the backend copy just got — a legacy/poisoned attribute still yields NaN in the renderer
samples.evidence: The change hardens the backend reader (`parseMarginFromEdge` in packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:353 falls back to DEFAULT_HEADER_MARGIN_FROM_EDGE for any non-finite attribute) and adds a backend test for the literal string `"undefined"`. The frontend store — the code that actually lays out and paints the header — still does `marginFromEdge: Number(attrs.marginFromEdge ?? '48')` at lines 526 and 532, so a node written by the pre-guard serializer (`marginFromEdge: "undefined"`) reads back as `NaN`. That NaN flows into `getHeaderYStart`/`getFooterYStart` (packages/docs/src/view/pagination.ts:260,274) and `doc-canvas.ts:272/318`, i.e. NaN geometry in the layout/paint path — exactly the failure mode the backend fix declares unacceptable. samples.summary: New `style.alignment` whitelist on PUT disagrees with the reader, which passes any string through — a read-modify-write (CLI pull/push) of a document holding a legacy alignment value now 400s
samples.evidence: `assertValidBlockStyle` rejects any `style.alignment` not in {left,center,right,justify}. But `parseBlockStyle` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:177 and the frontend copy at yorkie-doc-store.ts:244) accepts *any* string, including the literal "undefined" that the old unconditional serializer (`alignment: style.alignment` with an undefined value) could have persisted, and any other legacy token. So GET returns `style.alignment: "undefined"` and the very next PUT of that untouched body is rejected with 400 — the round-trip the controller comment calls "identity on the JSON shape" is no longer identity for such documents. The numeric fields were deliberately hardened on the read side (non-finite → default) but `alignment` was not, leaving validator and reader inconsistent.

samples.summary: `modifierXml` only skips `undefined`, so a `null` modifier is coerced to `0` — `<a:alpha val="0"/>` renders the color fully transparent
samples.evidence: `if (value === undefined) return ''; const n = Number(value);` — for `null`, `Number(null) === 0` is finite, so the attribute is emitted as `val="0"`. For `alpha` that means fully transparent (invisible text/fill) where the old code emitted an invalid `val="null"` that PowerPoint would ignore. The function's own doc comment says a non-numeric value should be dropped so "the base color [stays] intact"; `null` (and `''`, which also coerces to 0) defeats that. A `!Number.isFinite(n) || value === null` style check, or rejecting non-`number` typeof, would match the stated intent.

samples.summary: `serializeBlockStyle` / `serializeMarginFromEdge` coerce `null` (and `''`) to 0 instead of omitting the attribute
samples.evidence: `const value = Number(style?.[field]); if (style?.[field] !== undefined && Number.isFinite(value))` — `null` and `''` both coerce to a finite 0, so a field explicitly present as null is persisted as `"0"` rather than omitted and defaulted. Same in `serializeMarginFromEdge` (line 321-323: `Number(null) === 0` passes the `!== undefined` check → header pinned to offset 0) and in the frontend copy at packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:233. The stated contract is "emitted only when it carries a value the reader can invert"; null is not such a value, and the reader's default (e.g. lineHeight 1.5, marginFromEdge 48) is the intended result. The PUT validator rejects null for these fields, so the reachable callers are the non-validated ones (imports, hand-built documents).

samples.summary: Reworked cell-fill line still dereferences `cell.style` unconditionally, unlike the other two cell-background sinks which use `cell.style?.`
samples.evidence: `const cellFill = toDocxHexColor(cell.style.backgroundColor);` runs for every cell. The sibling painters treat `cell.style` as possibly absent — packages/docs/src/view/table-renderer.ts:175 (`cell.style?.backgroundColor`) and packages/docs/src/export/pdf-table-painter.ts:173 (`if (!cell.style?.backgroundColor) continue`) — and the backend validator added in this very change exists because payloads without `cell.style` reach the writer. verdict.reason: Every element of the finding checks out in the repo. Backend docs-tree.ts:318-324/353-358 gained both a serializer that omits absent/non-finite marginFromEdge and a parser that falls back to DEFAULT_HEADER_MARGIN_FROM_EDGE, with comments naming NaN header offsets as the failure being prevented. The frontend store still reads `Number(attrs.marginFromEdge ?? '48')` verbatim at yorkie-doc-store.ts:526 and :532 — the `??` covers only a missing attribute, so a stored `"undefined"` (or any non-numeric legacy string) yields NaN. That NaN is not normalized anywhere downstream: editor.ts:1931-1932 forwards it, doc-canvas.ts:272-278/318-322 uses it for clip rects, and pagination.ts:260/274 does raw arithmetic with it, so NaN geometry reaches the paint path. The writer half is also as described: yorkie-doc-store.ts:728, :769, :2724, :2732 unconditionally do `String(...marginFromEdge)`, and setDocument (:791-792 -> :2714) is fed untyped external content at apply-imported-content.ts:224 and docs-view.tsx:343, so an absent value is re-persisted as the literal "undefined" into the shared CRDT that the backend now defends against. No guard, caller-side normalization, or unreachable-path argument was found; the issue is runtime correctness (NaN state / broken render invariant), inside this lens.

finding.summary: PUT /content validation still leaves table-cell `style` and inline items unvalidated, and the writer dereferences both → HTTP 500 instead of 400
finding.evidence: The diff annotates `assertValidBlock` with the claim that shape validation covers what the writer dereferences ("Shape only. Style *values* are not constrained here…"). But the cell loop only checks `Array.isArray(cell.blocks)` (controller.ts:292-298) — it never checks `cell.style`. `serializeCellStyle` in packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:197-198 does `const s = cell.style; if (s.backgroundColor)`, so a payload like `{blocks:[{id:'t',type:'table',style:{},tableData:{columnWidths:[1],rows:[{cells:[{blocks:[]}]}]}}]}` throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'backgroundColor')` inside `doc.update` (controller.ts:163-165) → 500, the exact failure the guard's own header comment says it exists to prevent. Same gap for `inlines` items: only `Array.isArray(b.inlines)` is checked (controller.ts:309), while `buildInlineNode` does `inline.text.length` and `serializeInlineStyle(inline.style)` (docs-tree.ts:250,254), so `inlines:[null]` or `inlines:[{text:'x'}]` also 500s.

verdict.reason: Both allegedly-missing guards exist in the working tree, on the PUT validation path. (1) Table-cell `style` IS checked at docs-content.controller.ts:386 (`if (!cell.style || typeof cell.style !== 'object') throw new BadRequestException(...)`), with a comment at :382-385 explicitly citing `serializeCellStyle`'s unconditional deref. The finding's own repro payload `{cells:[{blocks:[]}]}` passes the array check at :371, the empty nested loop at :376 is a no-op, and :386 throws a 400 before docs-tree.ts:197 (`const s = cell.style`) is reached. (2) `inlines` elements ARE validated per item at :401-418: non-object/null at :403 (kills `inlines:[null]`), non-string `text` at :408 (guards `inline.text.length`, docs-tree.ts:251), and missing/non-object `style` at :413 (guards `serializeInlineStyle(inline.style)`, docs-tree.ts:254) — so `inlines:[{text:'x'}]` also 400s. The table arm returns at :393 so it correctly skips the inlines loop, and `buildBlockNode` (docs-tree.ts:260) only takes the table branch when `tableData` is present, which :353 requires. The reviewer's cited lines are stale for this tree: :291-297 is BLOCK_STYLE_NUMERIC_FIELDS and :308 is a doc comment; `assertValidBlock` spans :336-419, not 239-312.

finding.summary: `writeDocsRoot` still persists the literal string "undefined" for header/footer `marginFromEdge`, which reads back as NaN — the same poisoning the diff fixed for block styles
finding.evidence: The diff replaced the unconditional `String(style.lineHeight)` writes in `serializeBlockStyle` precisely because "writing those absent fields unconditionally would persist … the literal string `\"undefined\"` … which `parseBlockStyle` then reads back as `NaN`". Two functions below, `buildTreeChildren` still does `attributes: { marginFromEdge: String(document.header.marginFromEdge) }` (docs-tree.ts:316 and :326) with no guard, and `readDocsRoot` inverts it as `attrs.marginFromEdge ? Number(attrs.marginFromEdge) : DEFAULT_HEADER_MARGIN_FROM_EDGE` (docs-tree.ts:464-466) — `"undefined"` is truthy, so `Number("undefined")` = NaN reaches `header.marginFromEdge` and the layout engine. `assertValidDocsBody` never validates `body.header`/`body.footer` at all, so a PUT with `header: { blocks: [] }` (no marginFromEdge) is accepted and produces exactly this. The same unvalidated `document.header.blocks.map(...)` (docs-tree.ts:317) also TypeErrors on `header: {}` → 500.

verdict.reason: The code is not as described. (1) `buildTreeChildren` does not write `String(document.header.marginFromEdge)`; it calls `serializeMarginFromEdge` (docs-tree.ts:331, :341), which returns `{}` for `undefined`/non-finite values (docs-tree.ts:318-324) — no `"undefined"` string is ever persisted. (2) The reader is not `attrs.marginFromEdge ? Number(...) : DEFAULT`; `parseMarginFromEdge` (docs-tree.ts:353-358) uses `Number.isFinite`, so even a legacy poisoned `"undefined"` attribute reads back as `DEFAULT_HEADER_MARGIN_FROM_EDGE` (called at :491 and :498), covered by tests at docs-tree.spec.ts:184-221. (3) The claim that `assertValidDocsBody` never validates header/footer is false: it calls `assertValidHeaderFooter` for both (docs-content.controller.ts:258-259), which rejects a non-array `blocks` with a 400 (:270-274) and a non-finite `marginFromEdge` (:275-283), so `header: {}` cannot reach the `.map(...)` TypeError. Every element of the presence claim is absent from the working tree.

finding.summary: New block-style value validation covers only `alignment`; the numeric BlockStyle fields still accept arbitrary values that become NaN in layout
finding.evidence: `assertValidBlockStyle` validates `style.alignment` only. `writeDocsRoot` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:145) writes `marginTop: String(style.marginTop)` verbatim, and the read path does `partial.marginTop = Number(attrs.marginTop)` (docs-tree.ts:160) with `normalizeBlockStyle` being a bare spread (packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:272-274, no numeric coercion/guard). A PUT with `style: { marginTop: "abc" }` therefore lands NaN in the model, and `packages/docs/src/view/layout.ts:383` does `y += block.style.marginTop`, NaN-ing the cumulative y for every subsequent block — the whole document renders blank/garbled for every collaborator, with no way to fix it from the UI. Same exposure for `marginBottom`, `lineHeight`, `textIndent`, `marginLeft`.

verdict.reason: The claimed NaN path does not exist. `serializeBlockStyle` (docs-tree.ts:158-170) writes each of lineHeight/marginTop/marginBottom/textIndent/marginLeft only when `Number.isFinite(Number(value))`, so `style: { marginTop: \"abc\" }` is dropped rather than persisted as the reviewer's quoted `String(style.marginTop)`. `parseBlockStyle` (docs-tree.ts:172-189) likewise skips any attribute whose `Number(...)` is non-finite before calling `normalizeBlockStyle`, explicitly compensating for that function being a bare spread. Every write of block attributes goes through `serializeBlockStyle` (docs-tree.ts:265 table arm, :282 block arm, both reached from writeDocsRoot invoked at docs-content.controller.ts:164), and every read goes through `parseBlockStyle` (docs-tree.ts:396, 436, 457). Therefore no NaN can reach `layout.ts:383` via the PUT path, and the numeric fields are guarded even though the controller validator only checks `alignment`.

finding.summary: Block-style validation checks alignment values but still lets `style: {}` through, persisting the literal string "undefined" and NaN geometry into the CRDT
finding.evidence: The new test explicitly asserts `{ blocks: [{ id, type:'paragraph', style: {}, inlines: [] }] }` passes validation. `writeDocsRoot`'s `serializeBlockStyle` then produces `alignment: undefined` and `lineHeight: String(undefined) === 'undefined'` (docs-tree.ts:143-148); `parseBlockStyle` (line 159) does `Number('undefined') → NaN` and `normalizeBlockStyle` spreads that NaN over the default, so `marginTop`/`lineHeight` become NaN and `computeLayout`'s `y += block.style.marginTop` NaNs out the whole document layout. If the controller is now validating block-style *values*, the required numeric fields are the ones that actually corrupt the document when missing.

verdict.reason: The finding's premise — that `style: {}` reaches the CRDT as `alignment: undefined` and the literal string "undefined" for numeric fields, then reads back as NaN — is false in this working tree. `serializeBlockStyle` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:158-170) writes `alignment` only when `typeof style?.alignment === 'string'` (line 162) and writes each numeric field only when `style?.[field] !== undefined && Number.isFinite(value)` (lines 163-168), so `style: {}` serializes to `{}` — no "undefined" string is ever persisted. The read side is independently guarded: `parseBlockStyle` (lines 172-189) copies a numeric field only when `field in attrs` AND `Number.isFinite(value)` (lines 183-187) before handing the partial to `normalizeBlockStyle`, which is a bare spread over DEFAULT_BLOCK_STYLE (packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:272-273). So `style: {}` round-trips to DEFAULT_BLOCK_STYLE (alignment 'left', lineHeight 1.5, marginTop 0), and computeLayout's `y += block.style.marginTop` never sees NaN. Both call sites of serializeBlockStyle (docs-tree.ts:265 table, :282 non-table) use the guarded function, and buildTreeChildren routes body/header/footer blocks through buildBlockNode, so there is no bypassing path in this writer; the same defensive pattern is applied to marginFromEdge (lines 318-324, 353-358). The reviewer's cited line range (143-148) is the BLOCK_STYLE_NUMERIC_FIELDS constant, not the serializer body. Accepting `style: {}` is the documented partial-on-the-wire contract (doc comment lines 147-157), not a corruption hole.
